title: Reserved Inference Intake — Apex Synthesis
summary: Initial qualification for reserved GPU capacity. Customer runs latency-sensitive chat and embedding workloads; primary concerns are isolation, predictable p99 latency, burst handling, and data residency/KMS. Discussed prewarm strategies, fallback to hosted, and cost tradeoffs. Agreed to run a brief benchmark/POC and share security/compliance docs.
topics: burst profile and prewarm/hot pool strategy
next steps: benchmark POC and pricing
action_items: Samir Patel: Share dedicated pricing tiers + burst pricing spreadsheet (due 2026-11-12)
Lina Chow: Schedule 2-hour benchmark window; provide test harness and sample prompts (due 2026-11-13)
Marcus Reed: Provide expected qps/peak windows and current seq length distribution (due 2026-11-11)
next_steps: Run 48-hour benchmark using Apex test harness (Redwood to provide harness)
Exchange security questionnaire and SOC2 summary
Follow-up meeting to review benchmark results and sizing
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-08 15:30 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Chow (Redwood SE), Hannah Lee (CTO, Apex), Marcus Reed (Infra), Priya Kaul (PM)

Summary (auto): initial intake for reserved GPUs, isolation, burst strategy and compliance.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro from our side — i'm Samir, i'm the AE on this account, and Lina is our SE who usually helps run the benchmarks and sizing. how are you folks doing?
[00:12] Hannah: doing well, thanks. excited to see how reserved nodes would look for us, we have a big push in q1 and want to avoid noisy neighbors.
[00:20] Marcus: yeah, quick context — our infra is gke based, we run a mixture of hosted endpoints and some internal endpoints on prem; right now we’re hitting variability at peak and want predictability for chat features.
[00:34] Priya: hi, i'm priya — product — we need p99 latency guarantees for chat flows and lower token cost for embeddings.
[00:42] Lina: great, can you tell us about your current workload shape? burstiness, typical qps, sequence lengths?
[00:50] Marcus: typical steady qps is ~60 rps across our fleet, but we see headroom spikes to ~420 rps during launches and promotions, those last 5–15 minutes. seq len median is 240 tokens, tail goes up to 1024 for a small percent of requests.
[01:12] Samir: ok so you have a high tail and sharp short bursts — classic reserved capacity with hot-pool needs. what are your p99 targets?
[01:20] Priya: we want p95 < 250ms and p99 < 600ms for small chat context, for embeddings it's less strict but cost matters.
[01:30] Marcus: important note — anything that touches customer PII must stay in our VPC or on-prem, we have a KMS solution and need audit logs.
[01:42] Lina: that's totally reasonable. Redwood Dedicated supports VPC private nodes and integration with customer KMS/HSM. we have options — full private deployment where control plane is customer-managed, or dedicated in our cloud but with VPC isolation and tenant fencing.
[01:58] Hannah: can you clarify fencing? we want strict isolation: no cross-tenant memory leaks, no evictions for our reserved nodes during burst.
[02:08] Lina: sure. there are levels: logical tenancy via namespaces and strict cgroup isolation, and physical tenancy — pinned GPUs reserved to your account. for no-eviction guarantees we recommend reserved node pools with preemption disabled and hotpool prewarm for bursts.
[02:26] Marcus: is preemption truly disabled? what happens if there is hardware failure — do you fall back to hosted?
[02:34] Samir: good question — our SLA for Dedicated includes failover policies: if an entire node goes down, we can automatically route to a fallback hosted model with a compatible model variant and degrade gracefully. we also do live migration for some setups but that depends on private/onprem config.
[02:50] Priya: cost tradeoff there — fallback to hosted likely has higher per-token cost but keeps user experience up. curious about the economics.
[02:58] Samir: we'll share a cost model spreadsheet. elastic burst add-ons let you reserve baseline capacity and attach burst credits; during fallbacks the cost shifts and we flag it in the console.
[03:10] Hannah: what about model variants and quantization? can you run INT8 or q4 models for cost saving while keeping latency?
[03:18] Lina: yes — our runtime supports several quantization profiles. we typically benchmark your prompt set to pick the sweet spot — sometimes q4 is fine for embeddings but not for chat with structured outputs.
[03:30] Marcus: how do you handle KV cache warmups? that’s often a big contributor to p99 spikes for our workloads.
[03:36] Lina: we have prefix caching and sticky KV cache options for Dedicated. hotpool prewarm will keep warmed KV caches on standby for expected traffic windows. you can also control eviction windows to keep cache sticky for a tenant.
[03:50] Priya: we have regulatory requirement that full conversation logs are retained for 7 years, but encrypted at rest with our KMS. can your deployment meet that?
[03:58] Samir: yes — dedicated and private support customer-managed KMS and audit logs. we can share the SOC2 + data flow docs.
[04:06] Marcus: another practical thing — we run canary rollouts for model changes and need traffic split, A/B and automatic fallback. is that in the console?
[04:14] Lina: yes, rollouts and canaries are supported; you can pin routes to model versions. plus automatic fallback to the previous stable model or hosted variant on regression detection.
[04:26] Hannah: timeline: we have a q1 launch and need to sign a contract and be running by mid january. what does the onboarding look like?
[04:34] Samir: onboarding is typically 4–6 weeks for Dedicated with reserved GPUs — discovery, sizing, contract, provisioning, bench and rollout. for Private on-prem it's longer because of networking and KMS on boarding.
[04:44] Priya: we'll need to know the minimum commit and what burst headroom is available.
[04:50] Lina: minimum commit depends on GPU class; we can start with a small reserved slab (e.g., 4x A800-equivalent) and add burst capacity via warm pools or burst credits. you can also mix physical pinning for sensitive tenants and shared reserved for lower tiers.
[05:06] Marcus: what about multi-region? we need EU and US presence for data residency.
[05:12] Samir: Dedicated supports region pinning. for Private deployments we can deploy control plane in whichever region you prefer; we also support cross-region failover policies.
[05:24] Priya: on security — do you support SSO/SAML, RBAC, SCIM provisioning?
[05:30] Lina: yes to all. we integrate with common IDPs; audit trails include token-level traces.
[05:36] Marcus: any known limitations around onprem GPUs, like infiniBand or particular kernel versions?
[05:42] Lina: we have a hardware compatibility matrix — some custom kernels require tweaks. for onprem we run a short compatibility lab. we'll need CPU/mobo/driver details if you go that route.
[05:54] Hannah: i'd like to understand worst-case tail p99 during a burst if we rely solely on prewarm vs cold scaling.
[06:02] Lina: if you have a hotpool correctly sized to your peak concurrency, p99 is dominated by model decode time; for our served small chat models we've seen p99 under 300ms with prewarmed KV and batching tuned. cold starts without KV can spike to multiple seconds.
[06:20] Marcus: ok, can your warm pool maintain sticky KV when tenants rotate keys? we rotate keys every 90 days.
[06:28] Lina: yes, we can rewrap cache entries and support key rotation flows — there is a brief reconciliation window during rotation but we keep hotpool nodes alive to reduce cold penalties.
[06:40] Samir: touching back on cost — do you have a target spend range for this contract?
[06:46] Hannah: we are thinking $30k–$80k/month depending on node class and burst add-ons.
[06:54] Samir: that's in a typical range for mid-market Dedicated. we'll map that to specific GPU types and burst capacity in the spreadsheet.
[07:02] Priya: what's the SLA for latency and uptime for Dedicated?
[07:06] Samir: uptime SLA is 99.9% for Dedicated control plane and reserved nodes; latency SLOs are configurable by route, we can baseline with your target p99 and include alerts/penalties in an enterprise contract.
[07:18] Marcus: how does traffic routing work during regional failures? will requests go to hosted fallback in another region?
[07:24] Lina: routing is policy-driven — you can prefer local-region, then cross-region, then hosted fallback. we also support per-route fallbacks so you can keep core flows local.
[07:36] Hannah: what's the process for benching? if we want you to simulate our peak for 10 minutes, what is the recommended approach?
[07:44] Lina: we'll provide a harness. typical approach: provide sample prompt distribution, sequence length histogram, and target qps. we provision a sizing cluster, run sweeps for quantization/model variants, measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost. we recommend at least two 30–60 minute runs to capture caches and warmup.
[08:04] Marcus: can the harness replicate our KV cache behavior? we have reranking + multi-turn that stores context in a per-session KV.
[08:12] Lina: yes we can script sticky sessions and reuse KV across requests in the bench.
[08:18] Samir: any procurement or legal constraints we should be aware of?
[08:22] Hannah: we'll need to run a vendor security review and have a VAR-friendly contract template. plus we have data residency clauses.
[08:30] Samir: understood — we'll send our security questionnaire and SOC2 artifacts; legal can work with your procurement team on standard enterprise terms.
[08:38] Priya: one more thing: feature flags for model rollout — we need ability to do small percentage traffic and then ramp.
[08:44] Lina: yes that's native in our rollout UI and API.
[08:48] Marcus: what's the expected lead time to get reserved nodes provisioned after contract is signed?
[08:54] Samir: typically 2–3 weeks for reserved capacity in our cloud regions; on-prem will be different. if you need faster we can do a short-term hosted fallback while dedicated nodes are provisioned.
[09:06] Hannah: okay, let's get into a couple specific concerns: encryption in motion — do you support mTLS between our service and inference endpoints inside VPC?
[09:14] Lina: yes, mTLS is supported, and we can terminate inside the VPC for Private setups. For Dedicated in our cloud we support VPC peering and private endpoints over which you can enforce TLS and mTLS.
[09:28] Marcus: great. also, do you support bringing our own model or only your catalog? we plan to host some fine-tuned variants.
[09:36] Lina: you can bring models; we have onboarding for model binaries, compatibility checks, and we recommend doing a profiling run to tune kernels and quantization.
[09:46] Priya: any gotchas with ONNX or other format conversions?
[09:50] Lina: sometimes conversion affects accuracy; we keep eval harnesses to verify. we log per-model divergence and can recommend a non-quant path for sensitive outputs.
[10:00] Samir: at this point, sounds like a benchmark POC is the right next step?
[10:04] Hannah: yes. we'll need to align on what to measure and confirm our peak windows.
[10:10] Marcus: i'll pull QPS histograms and a sample request set.
[10:14] Priya: timeline: i'll want results before november 20th to line up procurement.
[10:20] Samir: fine — we can target finishing the benchmark by Nov 18 and review results on Nov 19. Lina — can you own the bench?
[10:28] Lina: yes, i'll spin up the harness and coordinate the 48-hour window.
[10:32] Samir: great — i'll send the pricing sheet and the security artifacts.
[10:36] Hannah: one quick architecture question — are reserved nodes automatically drained for maintenance or do you control that window?
[10:42] Lina: by default we schedule maintenance windows with customer approval; for Dedicated customers we give control over maintenance schedule and can avoid drain during declared peak windows.
[10:52] Marcus: curious about telemetry granularity — do you provide token-level cost breakdowns and per-route p99?
[10:58] Lina: yes — Console exposes token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, and model-level traces. you can also export traces to your observability stack.
[11:06] Priya: any recommendations for mix of reserved vs burst credits for a company with our pattern?
[11:12] Lina: given your frequent short spikes (5–15m to ~420 rps), we'd recommend baseline reserved to cover typical steady qps plus a warm-pool sized to handle 70–80% of your expected peak concurrency; remaining tail can be handled via burst credits or hosted fallback. the warm-pool helps keep KV warm which reduces p99 significantly.
[11:34] Marcus: what about eviction policies for warm pool in multi-tenant noisy neighbor scenarios?
[11:40] Lina: warm-pool instances can be dedicated to your tenant (no eviction) or shared with priority preemption rules. given your isolation needs i'd suggest dedicated warm-pool nodes for critical routes.
[11:52] Samir: ok, we're nearing the end. let's recap next steps and owners.
[11:58] Hannah: recap please.
[12:00] Samir: action items: Samir will send pricing and security artifacts; Lina will run/coordinate the benchmark harness; Marcus will share qps histograms and sample prompts; Priya will coordinate procurement timeline. target benchmark complete Nov 18 and follow-up on Nov 19.
[12:18] Marcus: sounds good. one last logistical Q — for the benchmark, do we need to open firewall rules or provide infra creds?
[12:24] Lina: we'll need limited access to a bastion or a test endpoint to run the harness; we can use ephemeral credentials and rotate them.
[12:34] Hannah: ok thanks, we'll get that to you.
[12:36] Samir: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[12:40] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: speakers occasionally overlap, some product names mis-transcribed. This is a standard Fireflies-style export with timestamps every ~10–60s.
